Convert between visual angle and screen pixels

Source: R/visual_angle.R
visual_angle_to_px.Rd

Converts a visual angle to the on-screen extent in pixels, and back, for a display viewed at a given distance. The extent is centred on the line of sight: an angle \(\theta\) spans \(2 d \tan(\theta / 2)\) on the screen, where \(d\) is the viewing distance. Use it to set distance thresholds such as the radius of fixation_revisits in degrees.

Usage

visual_angle_to_px(deg, distance, screen_size, screen_res)

px_to_visual_angle(px, distance, screen_size, screen_res)

Arguments

deg

Visual angle in degrees (vectorised).

distance

Eye-to-screen distance.

screen_size

Physical width (or height) of the screen, in the same units as distance.

screen_res

Screen resolution in pixels along the same dimension as screen_size.

px

Extent in pixels (vectorised).

Value

visual_angle_to_px() returns pixels; px_to_visual_angle() returns degrees.

Examples

# 2 degrees on a 52 cm wide, 1920 px display viewed from 60 cm
visual_angle_to_px(2, distance = 60, screen_size = 52, screen_res = 1920)
#> [1] 77.33936
px_to_visual_angle(77, distance = 60, screen_size = 52, screen_res = 1920)
#> [1] 1.991226
